Who We Are

From Conflict to Coexistence

Established7 April 2025 · Guwahati, Assam

A non-profit safeguarding the Asian Elephant and the people who share its land — the bridge between forest officials, vets and local communities.

Registered under the Indian Trusts Act, 1882
In-situ care · Amchang, Guwahati
The Challenge

A Crisis at the Forest's Edge

Assam holds India's second-largest elephant population. Shrinking habitat pushes herds and people into daily — often deadly — conflict.

5,828
wild elephants in Assam
Source: Elephant Population Estimation in Assam 2024, Assam Forest Department — up from 5,719 in 2017.
The Reality

High density and broken corridors fuel rising human-elephant conflict.

The Toll

Every year, both human and elephant lives are lost.

Our Mission

Turn conflict into lasting coexistence.

Critical Programme

Where Forest Meets City

  • Real-time tracking of elephant movements
  • Community-Based Early Warning Network
  • Safe-deterrence materials for villages
  • 24×7 coordination with Forest Department
50+ wild elephants roam the urban and rural forest edges of Amchang in Guwahati.
Strategic Focus

Amchang Wildlife Sanctuary

~50wild elephants in Amchang

Presently, we work in the urban and rural dwellings on the periphery of Amchang Wildlife Sanctuary, situated in Guwahati — a habitat where 50+ wild elephants meet a growing city. Where sanctuary meets street, specialized intervention is urgent.

On the Ground

What We Do

Serving as the vital bridge connecting the Forest Department, veterinary experts, and communities living alongside wild elephants.

Early Warning System

A robust community network providing real-time elephant tracking and alerts to protect lives on both sides.

Community Empowerment

Empowering locals through workshops, conservation ambassadors, community awareness, and non-lethal safe-deterrence materials.

In-Situ Medical Support

Ground intelligence helps veterinary teams treat injured elephants rapidly, without removing them from their habitat.

Rescue & Rehabilitation

Caring for, nourishing, and healing hurt or displaced elephants — from first response to full recovery.

Direct from the Field: Our Rescue & Recovery Missions

A Year-Long Fight to Save a Tusker

Working closely with the Forest Department and expert vets from Assam State Zoo, we've rescued numerous injured elephants — including a severely wounded tusker whose recovery from a devastating right hind-leg fracture spanned an entire year. Our team's on-ground intelligence and real-time updates ensured he received the precise care he needed to survive.

Our Core Impact on the Ground
Robust Tracking
We deployed our deep local network to track the injured elephant across challenging terrain — ensuring he was never lost to sight.
Combating Misinformation
We actively neutralized rumors and false alarms on the front lines, keeping the community calm and preventing panic.
Dedicated In-Situ Care
We managed his environment daily — monitoring his health and securing his food supply — until he achieved a full recovery.
And daily care brought one tusker home.
Deep local network — never lost from sight
Misinformation neutralized, community kept calm
Daily in-situ care bridged the gap to expert vets
Complex recovery spanning over a full year
Our Vision: The Road Ahead

What We Are Building

Assam holds India's second-largest wild elephant population. As habitats shrink, human-elephant conflict rises daily. Our mission is to be the vital bridge between elephants and local residents — building a future of peaceful coexistence.

Deploying Rapid Response & Tech

Equipping local volunteer teams and launching a 24/7 dedicated crisis helpline centre to respond instantly to conflicts.

Mobile Veterinary Task Force

A specialized mobile unit featuring expert veterinarians to treat both wild (with prior Forest Dept. permission) and domesticated elephants directly in the field.

Research & Community Livelihoods

Mapping critical elephant corridors to prevent encounters, while funding community-led conservation initiatives that support local families.
